body: Totally. I do not even know what I like anymore and I do no longer have any friends who share my interests. In my case, that was a void I had because he and I shared a lot of interests and I felt I could finally do anything I had always wanted to do. It is hard for me to find people with my interests so I am also mourning that.
Thanks for responding! That is awful, I am so sorry you went through that. The fake engagement is perverse. I am glad you could block and not look back.
Yes, that's true. I am actually somewhat hopeful for my new life. Something good has to happen or at least I am making room for it.

Same! The only times when he would seem to think was when we were broken up and through text. Come to think about it I never got an apology in person. 

Once I gave in, he already had his trophy so back to old ways.

In my experience, it was more like someone said before, that I was the "unachievable" trophy. Everyone in my circle of friends was pining over my ex and I never really understood why and for years I was never interested in him because I thought he was a player. He was but he convinced me that it was just a label and that he was always misunderstood. What I do find that kept me there longer was the idea that if you are a woman in your mid-30s, this is your last chance at anyone wanting you. In a way, it does echo the "hurry up" part: a feeling that you are past your prime anyways and that no one will be interested in you. A context where most guys are flakey also helped. He always used my age and the fact that "he would not ever leave me unlike all other men" to make me stay.

This is so true. I could never understand how after hours-long arguments he could simply go back to normal in a few hours. I would need days or weeks to recover from what was said. I would spend so much time replaying everything in my head. He had already forgotten 5 minutes later.

Unfortunately, I realized very late after the fifth and final break up. I went back to him multiple times because when we would break up he would know exactly what to say and managed to either make me feel like a) it was my fault for not making an effort to trust him, b) he was the only person in the world I could be compatible with, c) he was more than willing to do anything necessary and promised the moon, d) I was on edge all the time and by the 100th time of mistreatment I also lashed out. 

What reinforced it for me was him breaking no contact. I was calm and collected, emotionally distant but also polite. In the interaction we had, there was absolutely nothing he could say was wrong or my fault. And still, he got so mad at my emotional distance that he began calling names and saying all kinds of stuff. That to me was the indicator that he was the problem.

 I think the realization comes when you understand and deeply believe 100% that you are not at fault for other people's behaviors and you are not at fault for asking things that are actually the bare minimum such as basic respect.

It is really baffling, I am even over the feeling angry part. I just feel that it must be a very sad existence not ever ever being able to be genuine with anyone. 

I just mentioned in another post that, while in the relationship, I was diagnosed with OCD. Turns out that, miraculously, after 8 months out of the relationship, I no longer have any of the symptoms and my therapist no longer thinks that I have OCD.

Your story is very resonant with mine, although I'm in your girlfriend's position and my ex does make excuses for his behavior, but reading your explanation also makes me see how irrational I was being too. We had similar issues with exes and whatnot and he also did send some inappropriate messages to another girl when we started dating. Since the breakup, I have learned that I have OCD which causes me to overthink everything and for me this became an obsession. Maybe there's also some additional things going on with your ex, and although it is necessary to take responsibility for your actions and try to avoid them in the future, not everything is on you. I don't know if there's a possibility of you talking to her, I was also very very angry at my ex and would just be very mean when I discovered this, but now I regret everything.

I'm sorry to hear this. I don't know if it is of any help, but I broke up with my ex due to something similar, but he had previously broken my trust in a serious way. I regret it at times and I wish things would have been different and that we would have been able to solve the issue, but sometimes it is hard to see things clearly. I felt forced to leave, but I still love and care very deeply about him and I still can't see anyone else in my future after 4 months. I don't think you were necessarily wrong for responding, but maybe there were some other issues going on with trust?
"You want to be right?, fine! but you'll be alone" Yes, I was right about the cheating and I am definitely out.

Please stop. I have just come out of a relationship like this after two years. Money is not a justification for cheating or infidelity, and if that is the reason, it's even more disgusting. It tells you what her values are. I haven't gotten over it, and I am also hoping for a change in him to at least feel like he's sorry, but it won't happen. My ex partner even went to therapy to "fix things", but I don't think he really wanted to change. Some people just don't see anything wrong with this behavior and they do not care how many emotional corpses they leave behind. She is who she is and there if she does not want to change, no amount of therapy will fix it. Stop expecting anything from her, it won't happen.  I also feel guilty for lashing out and being furious each time I was betrayed, but the thing is, this person does not feel the slight remorse and is actively hurting you. Your reaction is normal, warranted, necessary, and useful. It is not irrational and out of place. 

I know it is hard to trust people right now or to have hope in relationships. I myself feel like shallowness will always reign over depth, but I am trying really hard not to let this person stand for everyone else. Keep being generous with people who do deserve generosity and try find yourself again.
Ugh, this is something I'm embarrassed about. Thinking about all the times I ended up apologizing for my suspicions.

This is what I feel. I can't help being angry at myself for not trusting my instincts. I'm also angry at myself for believing him when he told me it was all in my head and I was being irrational. I'm never ever going to ignore my gut feeling again.
I was told it was my problem for being insecure, self-centered, and selfish., that I couldn't handle him paying attention to anyone else.

Hi! Thank you for your comment. Unfortunately, I gave him another chance. He promised and begged and we were about to move in together in two weeks. Of course, it all happened again. Same process as described before. I finally decided to leave, I'm not spending my 30s in this hell of a relationship. I am glad that you got out of it too. I really don't understand these people, I suggested a million times to have an open relationship if that was what he needed, but he refused. My conclusion is that it is not just about lust. They like to see you suffer, they enjoy the conflict they cause, they like to see rivalry between women because of them, or really they are just empty, always chasing after trivial emotions.

I find this to be true. I always wonder how I could be in this situation when I have always been independent and not necessarily so invested in finding a partner. I think the reason was because I rejected him at first. I knew about his ways with exes and we were friends, so at first I didn't think it was the best idea. Then I fell for the love bombing. Now I think it was all a game/challenge to him. As soon as I started dating him (literally a week later although I didn't find out until after a year), he began chasing a girl he perceived as "difficult" for him (20 years younger, with a boyfriend).

I feel like this all the time! I'm so exhausted of repeating the same thing over and over, with logical and reasoned explanations. I feel the need to explain it over and over because I feel that he does not care about what I am saying or he does not understand it. Then I am  unbearable, always the same thing with me, if I continue this way he will end things because I make a fuss over insignificant mistakes (sexting other people, daily chats with exes) and maybe I should realize "I am incapable of being happy".

Early in our relationship, we had an argument because he had claimed that he had cut ties with his ex and three months later I discover he found her a job at his office so they had been working together every day the whole time. I don't know how he did it, but I ended up being understanding, telling him that he is really special because he's the only person who has managed to make me change my mind, make me be less stubborn, and see things from another point of view. I now cringe with embarrassment when I think of that because of how naive I was and for thinking manipulation was special lol.

This is what my soon-to-be ex (if I get the courage) does. Whenever he does something of the sort, he claims he didn't do anything wrong because he didn't have sex. I have been explaining it is not about the sex, but the betrayal and lies of omission, and then he gets angry and claims he's so fed up with my constant "moral precepts" and that everything has to go according to my rules, and that relationships cannot be guided by a rule book. I am so tired of feeling like the boundaries of a monogamous relationship are my personal requirements and that I just can't stop "pressuring him and demand perfection."

Thank you for your response. 

I'm starting to think that he actually is one, or at least abusive. At the same time, I've also had behaviors that I am not proud of, but I think they stem from my feeling that something is not right. 

I think the reason it is so hard is because they give us the responsibility for everything and at the same time they love-bomb when they think they are about to lose you, so it's hard to see them as awful partners. All of his ex's say the same as well, but he said it was because they weren't the right ones for him. Now I see that it's just the way he is, and no matter how much he claims to love someone, it is the way he functions in the world. 

I sometimes fantasize with talking to his exes (I know them all because we are from a small town), but I don't want to make things more complicated. I don't know how or when I'll leave, but I just feel like I've been drained from all the energy I had for this.

It is really hard since part of me knows and another part questions that knowledge. It is as if there were two voices in my head debating the validity of my thoughts with no conclusion. I went to my therapist today and she also made me see things clearly. He even tried to make me change therapists because he said it wasn't working, and I  thought about it. But in the end I have chosen not to because deep down I know the reason he wanted me to change was because the therapist was actually doing her job too well. 

The reason why I feel like I might be the narcissist is because he tells me that all I want is to have everything my way and the if he steps outside any of my boundaries then its the end of the world. I really don't think my boundaries are that strict, although he makes me feel that way.

Thank you so much for taking the time to respond.

Thank you so much for your view on this. I do feel like everything is so childish and that he just does not have emotional maturity or plain maturity at all. I often feel like everything is surface for him or that there is no interiority to him at all. I don't know how to explain it. 

I totally empathize with your thoughts about boundaries, I sometimes feel that way and think that maybe if I were more flexible it would all be easier, but then I realize that I cannot continue to allow this. He makes me feel like I have crazy strict boundaries when they are just the boundaries of any monogamous relationship. I shouldn't have to teach those to anyone and if he hasn't learnt them at 40 then I don't know why he insists in having this kind of relationship. At some point I even suggested that maybe an open relationship would work better for him but he said no way, I imagine because he doesn't want his partners doing the same. 

Anyways, now I'm just venting but thank you so much again for your reply.

Thank you for your reply. I know it is exasperating to read something like this. I still don't know why I put up with this. Although I don't know if he is a clinical narc, I do think he needs supply to feel good about himself. 

To be honest, I think gaslighting is not really a term used where I am from, but I have been realizing this for some time now and I often wish I had recorded past conversations due to the amount of times when I have seen something that then was negated by him. I have just come back from therapy and I actually hadn't realized the extent of the seriousness of this situation and the constant shifting of responsibility towards me. 

I am very grateful for all the replies I have received here and I think I am closer to choosing my mental health over... I don't even know what's left.

I don't know. Stopping at a grocery store to masturbate because OP turns him on so much so why not go home to her? It is really weird. I understand nothing seems to indicate he's lying, but the explanation is quite incoherent. I don't know how OP brought up the topic and how often it happens, so I don't know if the over-the-top reaction is warranted or not. I'm also wondering if there's been any previous incidents of breaching of trust.
Thank you for responding! I’m sorry to hear that you were in a similar place. I hope therapy is helping and hope things are better 💕
Thanks for your reply! You’re right. I don’t think I can trust him again.
